question.text: In GP-LP nomenclature used in foreign LLP-form AIFs, who are 'Limited Partners' and who is the 'General Partner'?

answer.text: GP = investors; LPs = manager and sponsor.
GP = custodian; LPs = auditors of the fund.
GP = the manager/sponsor (day-to-day control + unlimited liability); LPs = contributing investors (passive, capital only, limited liability).

explanation.text: The Logic: In the LLP-form (predominantly US/Cayman) AIF model, the GP (General Partner) is the manager or sponsor - runs day-to-day operations and traditionally carries unlimited liability for GP acts. LPs (Limited Partners) are passive capital providers whose liability is capped at their committed capital. The Trap: Inverting GP/LP roles, or mapping to SEBI/custodian/auditor, is nonsensical but tempting to candidates unfamiliar with the convention. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A both use GP/LP terminology. XXI-B uses 'portfolio manager' and 'client' instead. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating with a US-based LP used to GP-LP language, translate into Indian trust-AIF equivalents: Manager = GP, Beneficiary/Contributor = LP, Trustee = independent fiduciary.
